text: Cold storage of tissue is limited by progressive cell loss.
We asked whether Kelmorin, a synthetic compound, protects rat kidney slices during cold storage.
Slices were kept in cold buffer for one day with or without Kelmorin.
Viability after storage was higher with Kelmorin (71%) than in untreated slices (52%).
Lactate release was lower in treated slices (3.1 mmol/L) than in untreated slices (4.8 mmol/L).
Tissue water content did not differ between the groups (78% and 79%).
Caspase activity tended to be lower after Kelmorin treatment (1.9 versus 2.4 units), which may indicate reduced apoptosis.
Kelmorin was tested only in rat kidney slices and not in whole organs.
